method: Thesis exposure = sum over open theses of posterior x value-pool weight (mandatory infrastructure 1.0, pricing power / scarce 0.9, abundant -0.3, new risk -0.6, loses pricing power -1.0). Final = exposure x (0.5 + opportunity/100) x (1 + gap/100) x technical readiness (trend template) x attention (not-priced +15%, crowded -20%). 'ready' = passes the book's entry gate today.

picks.why: Highest thesis exposure in the book (7.17) and the only name that sits in the value pool of both T-004 (97% posterior, power as the binding constraint on AI capacity) and T-003 (85.5%, private substitution for degrading public reliability), with equipment OEMs flagged as both 'scarce' and 'gains_pricing_power'. Despite narrative at 77, pricing is only 45 against reality 62 — a +17 expectations gap, meaning the market is paying utility-equipment multiples for what the theses say is a multi-year pricing-power franchise. The gap exists because the stock is in a basing/downtrend (technical 50, not ready): recent AI-capex credit stress has de-rated the whole electrification complex faster than orders have changed.
picks.entry_condition: Wait for the base to resolve — reclaim of the prior structure with technical_stage flipping out of basing into emerging/stage2; or buy earlier only on a confirming T-003 signal: a PJM capacity auction or state PUC order that rate-bases data-centre load rather than socialising it.
picks.key_risk: T-004's own next_signal flags the neocloud/vendor-financed GPU counterparty default as the live danger; a credit event there truncates announced-MW and turns GEV's backlog from scarce capacity into cancellable orders, which the current basing pattern is already sniffing.

picks.why: The only candidate in the set flagged buy_readiness 'ready' — technical 75 and emerging — and it carries the cleanest fundamental base here (reality 79, the highest score in the file) with a +17 expectations gap at pricing 62. It sits in four value pools as pure 'scarce': copper/conductors under T-004 (97%), transition metals under T-006 (89.1%), raw materials under T-003 (85.5%), and scarce physical stores of value under T-009. Thesis exposure is only 2.99 because it touches few layers, but every layer it touches is unambiguously scarce rather than merely mandatory — a cleaner claim on the electron bottleneck than the equipment names.
picks.entry_condition: Buy now on the emerging-stage setup; add on confirmation that the T-004 power constraint is still binding (GPU spot rental and HBM contract pricing failing to fall for a fourth consecutive month).
picks.key_risk: It is a commodity proxy with jurisdictional concentration — a December hike with the 10-year above 5% (the T-006 cancellation trigger) hits copper demand expectations directly, and the T-009 gold/hard-asset leg at 60.3 posterior is the weakest thesis supporting it.

picks.why: Largest expectations gap among the industrials at +27 with pricing at 30 against reality 57 — the market is explicitly not paying for the labour-scarcity rent. It is the top-weighted name for T-007 (92.1%, repair/renovation and retrofit gaining pricing power) and carries T-006 (89.1%) field-labour aggregation and skilled human capital as scarce, plus T-004 transmission/substation EPC. The disconnect is behavioural: the stock trades as an AI-capex derivative, so the capex scare crushed pricing (technical 25, basing) while the T-007 housing-format and MRO leg, which has nothing to do with data centres, is independently intact.
picks.entry_condition: Late-January Q4 prints and 2027 guidance: enter if backlog duration extends past 18 months with craft labour explicitly named as the binding constraint — the exact test T-006's next_signal says is still unmet.
picks.key_risk: Technical score 25 is the worst-positioned name I am recommending; if the same January guidance shows a disclosed data-centre project cancellation, crews get released and the scarcity rent inverts fast at a stock that has no technical support beneath it.

picks.why: Same value pools as EME (T-007 at 1.66, T-006 at 1.60) but with a better fundamental base — reality 67 versus EME's 57 — and a comparable +29 expectations gap at pricing 38. Narrative is only 60, so unlike GEV this is not a story stock with a lagging price; it is a cash-generative crew-owning contractor the market has simply stopped re-rating. Technical 38 and basing means the de-rating is still in progress, which is the price of the gap.
picks.entry_condition: Pair-trigger with EME: enter on the late-January guidance test (18-month backlog, named craft constraint, wage-escalation clauses) or earlier on a technical flip out of basing with attention still under 55.
picks.key_risk: Comfort Systems is the most data-centre-levered of the mechanical contractors; the T-006 scenario where a neocloud credit event converts delay into cancellation hits its mix hardest, and reality 67 would re-rate down quickly on a single guidance cut.

picks.why: The widest expectations gap in the entire candidate set at +34, with pricing 24 against reality 58 and narrative at 44 — the lowest narrative score here, meaning no one is telling this story at all. It is the top T-007 name outside the contractors (rental operations infrastructure and factory-built housing finance as mandatory_infrastructure, 92.1% posterior) and sits in T-002's scarce layers for identity/fraud-graph data and risk pricing (78.7%). The market is pricing a mortgage-origination cyclical; the theses price a toll on the format shift to rentals, BTR and manufactured housing — volumes that still need underwriting and comparables regardless of whether anyone buys a traditional home.
picks.entry_condition: Technical score is 0 — do not anticipate. Require a base to form (technical out of 0, attention still under 55) plus the T-007 confirmation: a third consecutive sub-26% first-time-buyer print in the NAR profile.
picks.key_risk: Technical 0 means something fundamental is being repriced that the reality score of 58 has not caught — most plausibly pricing-power/regulatory pressure on the score monopoly, which would hit the exact rent the T-002 risk-pricing layer assumes is scarce.

picks.why: The only security name here with a positive expectations gap (+8, pricing 59 vs reality 67) and the highest opportunity score in the file at 66 — CRWD (-19), PANW (-20), ZS (-6) and NET (-14) carry identical thesis exposure of 5.05 but are already paid for. All four sit in T-002's 'enterprise security platforms as mandatory_infrastructure' (78.7%) plus T-004 trust-and-attestation and T-005 biometric governance; FTNT is simply the one where the market has not yet capitalised the mandatory-infrastructure status. Technical 62 and emerging, attention 72 — the highest attention reading in the set, which is a warning the gap may close quickly.
picks.entry_condition: Enter on the emerging stage confirming to stage2 uptrend, or on the T-002 next_signal: Palo Alto's mid-November and CrowdStrike's early-December prints disclosing agent/AI-security as a separate ARR or attach-rate line (which validates the layer for the whole group and most benefits the cheapest member).
picks.key_risk: T-002's decisive test is vendor revenue in a year where total IT spend grows under 2%; if agent-security gets bundled with no pricing attached across both PANW and CRWD, the 'mandatory infrastructure becomes priced infrastructure' leg fails and FTNT's gap is just a cheap firewall vendor, not a mispricing.

picks.why: The only utility in the set and the only name carrying an explicit headwind (-0.09 from T-003's 'regulated utilities with residential-heavy rate base lose pricing power'), yet it still scores +2.13 from T-004 where firm dispatchable generation adjacent to load gains pricing power and powered land/interconnection/water rights become scarce at 97% posterior. Gap is +12 (pricing 47, reality 59) with narrative at 83 — the story is loud but the price is not reflecting it, which is unusual and typically means the market is discounting the regulatory outcome rather than the asset.
picks.entry_condition: Enter only on a FERC or state PUC order that makes behind-the-meter co-location a standard tariffed product (T-004 next_signal #3), or on a post-midterm rate docket that allocates rather than socialises data-centre cost; otherwise stay out while technical is basing.
picks.key_risk: T-004 explicitly names 'community/ratepayer political risk' as a new_risk for this exact layer — a ratepayer backlash that socialises AI load costs onto residential bills simultaneously triggers the T-003 headwind and caps the T-004 upside, which is why narrative 83 has not converted into price.

memo.portfolio_note: This book is one macro bet expressed three ways: the electron/physical-constraint complex (GEV, SCCO, EME, FIX, D) driven by T-004 at 97% and T-006/T-007 in the high 80s–90s, a single cheap option on security-as-mandatory-infrastructure (FTNT), and one uncorrelated format-shift toll (FICO). The concentration risk is blunt — five of seven names rise and fall with whether AI data-centre capex holds, and T-006's own next_signal names the December FOMC plus the first disclosed project cancellation as the trigger that converts scarcity rent into crew release. I deliberately excluded CRWD, PANW, ATKR, AAPL and NET despite strong technicals because their expectations gaps are -19 to -27: the theses are right and already paid for, which is not an edge. Note the structural tension: every name I like on expectations (EME 25, FIX 38, FICO 0, GEV 50) is technically broken, and the only technically ready name (SCCO) has the thinnest exposure — so sizing should be staged, with SCCO funded now and the rest on confirmation. What changes the list: a neocloud or vendor-financed GPU credit event would force me to cut EME, FIX and GEV outright and keep only FICO and FTNT; conversely, a PJM/PUC ruling that rate-bases AI load would justify doubling the GEV and D weights and dropping the contractor duplication to one name.
